picks.editorial_note: A combined $1.1B+ commitment from Georgia Tech and Emory is one of the largest university AI investments on record, positioning the Atlanta region as a national AI hub and signaling how deeply institutions are now betting on AI infrastructure and talent.
picks.title: Georgia Tech and Emory Invest More Than $1B in AI to Drive State’s Jobs, Economic Growth

picks.editorial_note: A White House-brokered consortium of 15 universities across 10 states to pool supercomputing resources marks a significant federal push to democratize AI compute access and reflects a new model of regional academic collaboration on national AI strategy.
picks.title: UK partners with regional universities in super intelligence computing consortium

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's leadership of a DOE Genesis Mission award applying autonomous AI discovery to catalysis research shows the federal government's flagship AI science initiative translating into concrete lab-level work with real energy and chemistry implications.
picks.title: SLAC to lead a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project for Super Intelligence (SI)-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis

picks.editorial_note: Phase II Genesis Mission funding for Berkeley Lab's accelerator-design AI project shows sustained federal investment in using AI to optimize core physics infrastructure, a rare case of 'AI for AI's enabling tools' at a national lab.
picks.title: Super Intelligence for Particle Accelerators Gets Another Boost

picks.editorial_note: Georgia Tech's Nexus supercomputer, built with a $20M NSF award and University of Illinois partnership, opens next-generation AI compute to researchers nationwide, directly expanding the research community's access to scarce high-performance infrastructure.
picks.title: Georgia Tech Opens Supercomputer to Researchers Nationwide

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's DOE-backed SPIRE project to build autonomous 'self-driving laboratories' represents a genuine shift toward AI agents independently running photon-science experiments, a notable step for scientific-discovery automation.
picks.title: SLAC leads new project to build the self-driving laboratory of the future

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's two Genesis Mission awards applying AI to microelectronics and quantum information science extend the DOE's national AI-for-science push into chip design and quantum research, areas with direct national competitiveness implications.
picks.title: Fermilab to lead two new Genesis Mission awards to accelerate development of microelectronics and quantum

picks.editorial_note: Google.org's $5M, three-year commitment to Georgia Tech for democratizing AI access in scientific research is a notable industry-to-academia funding flow aimed at broadening who can use advanced AI tools for discovery.
picks.title: Georgia Tech Receives $5 Million From Google.org to Expand Access to AI for Scientific Discovery

picks.editorial_note: An R&D 100 Award — one of the most prestigious innovation prizes in applied science — for a multi-lab AI-driven facility monitoring system validates a real-world deployed AI safety technology with cross-laboratory impact.
picks.title: NNSS collaborates on LANL's R&D 100 Award-winning Persistent DynAMICS project - Nevada National Security Site

picks.editorial_note: CMU's Nature-published Ataraxos system beating top humans at Stratego, a game defined by hidden information, pushes the frontier of AI decision-making under uncertainty, a capability with broad implications beyond gaming.
picks.title: CMU Researchers Develop AI That Tackles Hidden Information in Stratego
